description: Complete reference for the Sugar programming language

sections.title: Basic Syntax
sections.description: Sugar uses a clean, expressive syntax with explicit type annotations and clear block delimiters.

subsections.title: Comments
subsections.description: Single-line comments start with // and extend to the end of the line.
examples: // Comments use double slashes and extend to end of line

subsections.title: Statements
subsections.description: Sugar programs consist of statements. Each statement performs an action.

subsections.title: Blocks
subsections.description: Code blocks are delimited by do and end keywords.
examples:
if $condition$ do
    // Block content
    IO:PRINT:("Inside block")
end

sections.title: Data Types
sections.description: Sugar has a rich type system with both primitive and complex types.

types.name: Arrays
types.description: Ordered collections of elements of the same type

sections.title: Collection Methods
sections.description: Built-in methods for manipulating arrays, strings, and maps using method call syntax

subsections.title: Array Methods
subsections.description: Methods available on array types #[#type]

methods.name: :LENGTH:
methods.description: Returns the number of elements in the array

methods.name: :GET:
methods.description: Gets the element at the specified index

methods.name: :SET:
methods.description: Sets the element at the specified index

methods.name: :ADD:
methods.description: Adds an element to the end of the array

methods.name: :INSERT:
methods.description: Inserts an element at the specified index

methods.name: :REMOVE:
methods.description: Removes and returns the element at the specified index

methods.name: :CONTAINS:
methods.description: Checks if the array contains the specified value

methods.name: :INDEX_OF:
methods.description: Returns the index of the first occurrence of value, or -1 if not found

methods.name: :SLICE:
methods.description: Returns a new array containing elements from start to end index

methods.name: :REVERSE:
methods.description: Reverses the array in place

methods.name: :SORT:
methods.description: Sorts the array in place

methods.name: :SUM:
methods.description: Returns the sum of all numeric elements

methods.name: :MAP:
methods.description: Applies a function to each element and returns new array

methods.name: :FILTER:
methods.description: Returns new array with elements that pass the test function

methods.name: :REDUCE:
methods.description: Reduces the array to a single value using accumulator function
examples: DEF sum #int = numbers :REDUCE: (FUNC (acc #int, x #int) -> acc + x, 0)

methods.name: :ANY:
methods.description: Returns true if any element passes the test function

methods.name: :ALL:
methods.description: Returns true if all elements pass the test function

methods.name: :SLICE:
methods.description: Returns a new array containing elements from start to end index

methods.name: :SUM:
methods.description: Returns the sum of all numeric elements in the array

methods.name: :SORT:
methods.description: Sorts the array in place in ascending order

methods.name: :TO:
methods.description: Converts the value to the specified type

methods.name: :UPPER:

methods.name: :LOWER:

methods.name: :ADD:

methods.name: :INDEX_OF:

methods.name: :REVERSE:

methods.name: :REMOVE:

methods.name: :SPLIT:

subsections.title: Map Methods
subsections.description: Methods available on map types #{#key_type, #value_type}

methods.name: :GET:
methods.description: Gets the value associated with the specified key

methods.name: :SET:
methods.description: Sets the value for the specified key

methods.name: :HAS_KEY:
methods.description: Checks if the map contains the specified key

methods.description: Returns an array of all keys in the map

methods.name: :VALUES:

sections.title: Variables & Assignment
sections.description: Variable declaration and assignment in Sugar

subsections.title: Variable Declaration with DEF
subsections.description: All variables must be declared with explicit types

subsections.title: Assignment with :=
subsections.description: Use := to assign new values to existing variables

sections.title: Conditionals
sections.description: Conditional execution with if, elif, and else

subsections.title: Basic If Statements
subsections.description: Conditions must be enclosed in $ symbols
examples:
if $x > 5$ do
    IO:PRINT:("x is greater than 5")
end

subsections.title: If-Else Statements
examples:
if $age >= 18$ do
    IO:PRINT:("Adult")
else do
    IO:PRINT:("Minor")
end

subsections.title: Elif Chains
examples:
if $score >= 90$ do
    IO:PRINT:("Grade: A")
elif $score >= 80$ do
    IO:PRINT:("Grade: B")
elif $score >= 70$ do
    IO:PRINT:("Grade: C")
else do
    IO:PRINT:("Grade: F")
end

sections.title: Loops
sections.description: Iteration with while and for loops

subsections.title: While Loops
examples:
DEF count #int = 0
while $count < 5$ do
    IO:PRINT:(count)
    count := count + 1
end

subsections.title: For Loops
subsections.description: Iterate over collections or ranges
examples:
for DEF num #int in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] do
    IO:PRINT:(num)
end

for DEF i #int in RANGE(10) do
    IO:PRINT:(i)
end

for DEF char #char in "Hello" do
    IO:PRINT:(char)
end

sections.title: Concurrency & Tasks
sections.description: Parallel execution using SPAWN and Task management

subsections.title: Spawning Tasks
subsections.description: Create and execute functions concurrently using SPAWN

subsections.title: Task Types
subsections.description: Tasks are handles to concurrently executing functions

types.name: #Task
types.description: Handle to a spawned task that can be joined or cancelled
examples:
DEF task #Task = SPAWN FUNC() #int
    RETURN 42
end

types.name: #Token
types.description: Cancellation token for cooperative task cancellation
examples:
FUNC long_running(cancellable_token #Token) #int
    if $cancellable_token :CANCELLED:()$ do
        RETURN 0
    end
    // ... rest of computation
end

subsections.title: Task Operations
subsections.description: Methods available on Task objects for control and synchronization

methods.name: :JOIN:
methods.description: Waits for the task to complete and returns its result
examples: DEF task #Task = SPAWN FUNC() #int RETURN 42 end

methods.name: :TIMEOUT_JOIN:
methods.description: Waits for task completion with timeout (milliseconds), returns true if completed
examples:
if $completed$ do
    DEF result #int = task :JOIN:()
end

methods.name: :DONE:
methods.description: Checks if the task has completed without blocking

methods.name: :CANCEL:
methods.description: Attempts to cancel the task execution

methods.name: :CANCELLED:
methods.description: Returns true if the task was cancelled

methods.name: :SUCCESS:
methods.description: Returns true if the task completed successfully (without error)
examples:
if $task :SUCCESS:()$ do
    DEF result #int = task :JOIN:()
else do
    IO:PRINT:("Task failed: " + task :ERROR:())
end

methods.name: :ERROR:
methods.description: Returns the error that occurred in the task (only valid if task failed)
examples:
if $!task :SUCCESS:()$ do
    DEF error_msg #str = task :ERROR:()
    IO:PRINT:("Task failed: " + error_msg)
end

patterns.name: Parallel Computation
patterns.description: Run multiple tasks and collect results
patterns.example:
DEF task1 #Task = SPAWN FUNC() #int RETURN compute_heavy() end
DEF task2 #Task = SPAWN FUNC() #int RETURN compute_heavy() end
DEF result1 #int = task1 :JOIN:()
DEF result2 #int = task2 :JOIN:()

patterns.name: Background Processing
patterns.example:
SPAWN FUNC() #void
    while $true$ do
        monitor_system()
        Time:SLEEP:(5000)
    end
end

patterns.name: Timeout Operations
patterns.example:
DEF task #Task = SPAWN FUNC() #int RETURN slow_operation() end
DEF completed #bool = task :TIMEOUT_JOIN: (5000)
if $!completed$ do
    task :CANCEL:()
    IO:PRINT:("Operation timed out")
end

sections.title: Module System & Imports
sections.description: Code organization and reuse through module imports

subsections.title: Import Statements
subsections.description: Import functions, classes, and variables from other Sugar files

subsections.title: Dotted Name Imports
subsections.description: Import specific symbols using dotted notation
rules: Module names correspond to .sugar file names
Symbols can be functions, classes, variables, or constants
Use dotted notation to specify the exact symbol to import
Imported symbols become available in the current scope

subsections.title: Module Structure
subsections.description: How to structure code for imports
guidelines: Classes, functions, and variables can all be imported
Module file names should use snake_case

example_module.content:
// math_utilities.sugar
DEF PI #float = 3.14159

CLASS Calculator
    STATIC FUNC add(a #int, b #int) #int
        RETURN a + b
    end
end

FUNC square(x #float) #float
    RETURN x * x
end

usage_example.content:
// main.sugar
import math_utilities.PI
import math_utilities.Calculator
import math_utilities.square

DEF area #float = PI * square(5.0)
DEF sum #int = Calculator:add:(10, 20)

sections.title: Error Types
sections.description: Built-in and custom error types for exception handling

subsections.title: Built-in Error Types
subsections.description: Standard error types provided by the language

types.name: Error
types.description: Base error type that all errors extend

properties.name: message
properties.description: Error message describing what went wrong

examples:
CATCH e #Error do
    IO:PRINT:("Error: " + e.message)
end

types.name: ValueError
types.description: Raised when a function receives an argument of the correct type but inappropriate value
examples:
CATCH e #ValueError do
    IO:PRINT:("Value error: " + e.message)
end

subsections.title: Custom Error Types
subsections.description: User-defined error types for specific error conditions
subsections.syntax:
TYPE ErrorName EXTENDS Error
    additional_properties
end
examples:
TYPE MyError EXTENDS Error
    message #str
end

FUNC risky_operation() #void
    THROW MyError("Custom error occurred!")
end

TRY
    risky_operation()
CATCH e #MyError do
    IO:PRINT:("Caught: " + e.message)
end

subsections.title: Function Composition
subsections.description: Combining simple functions to build complex operations

DEF.description: Declares a new variable with an explicit type annotation and initial value
rules: Variable names must start with a letter or underscore
Initial value must match the declared type
Variables are mutable after declaration (use := for assignment)

FUNC.description: Declares a function with parameters and return type
examples:
FUNC add(a #int, b #int) #int
    RETURN a + b
end

FUNC print_message() #void
    IO:PRINT:("No return value")
end

CLASS.description: Defines a new class with properties and methods
examples:
CLASS Person
    PUBLIC name #str
    PRIVATE age #int
    
    PUBLIC CONSTRUCTOR(name #str, age #int) #void
        THIS.name := name
        THIS.age := age
    end
    
    PUBLIC FUNC get_age() #int
        RETURN THIS.age
    end
end

if.description: Conditional execution based on boolean expression
rules: Condition must be enclosed in $ symbols
examples:
if $x > 5$ do
    IO:PRINT:("x is greater than 5")
end

for.syntax: for DEF variable #type in collection do ... end
examples:
for DEF num #int in numbers do
    IO:PRINT:(num)
end

for DEF i #int in RANGE(10) do
    IO:PRINT:(i)
end

for DEF i #int in RANGE(0, 20) do
    IO:PRINT:(i)
end

MATCH.description: Matches an expression against multiple patterns

examples:
MATCH coordinates
CASE (0, 0) do
    IO:PRINT:("Origin")
CASE (#int x, #int y) do
    IO:PRINT:("Point at " + x + ", " + y)
end

MATCH numbers
CASE [] do
    IO:PRINT:("Empty array")
CASE [#int first] do
    IO:PRINT:("Single element: " + first)
CASE [1, 2, #int rest] do
    IO:PRINT:("Starts with 1, 2")
end

MATCH person
CASE {name: "Alice", age: #int age} do
    IO:PRINT:("Alice is " + age + " years old")
CASE {name: #str name, age: #int age} if $age >= 18$ do
    IO:PRINT:(name + " is an adult")
end

MATCH value
CASE #int n if $n < 0$ do
    IO:PRINT:("Negative number")
CASE #int n if $n > 100$ do
    IO:PRINT:("Large number")
CASE #[#int] arr if $arr :LENGTH:() > 3$ do
    IO:PRINT:("Long array")
end

MATCH value
CASE 0 do
    IO:PRINT:("Zero")
CASE #int x if $x > 10$ do
    IO:PRINT:("Large")
CASE (1, "a") do
    IO:PRINT:("Tuple match")
DEFAULT do
    IO:PRINT:("Other")
end

import.description: Imports functions, classes, or variables from other Sugar modules

examples:
TYPE Person

INTERFACE.description: Defines a contract that classes can implement
examples:
INTERFACE Drawable
    FUNC draw() #void
    FUNC resize(width #int, height #int) #bool
end

TRY
    risky_operation()
CATCH error #ValueError do
    IO:PRINT:("Error: " + error.message)
end

CATCH error #ValueError do

end

FINALLY.description: Code that runs regardless of whether an error occurred

THROW.description: Throws an error to be caught by error handling blocks

SPAWN.description: Executes a function concurrently and returns a Task handle
examples: DEF task #Task = SPAWN FUNC() #int RETURN compute() end

RETURN.description: Returns a value from a function

THIS.description: References the current instance in class methods

SUPER.description: References the parent class constructor or methods
examples: SUPER:(x, y, color)  // Call parent constructor

STATIC.description: Declares a static method that belongs to the class, not instances
examples:
STATIC FUNC create_default() #MyClass
    RETURN MyClass("default")
end

PUBLIC.description: Makes class members accessible from outside the class

PRIVATE.description: Makes class members accessible only within the class

PROTECTED.description: Makes class members accessible within the class and subclasses

OVERRIDE.description: Overrides a parent class method in a subclass

complete.title: Object-Oriented Example
complete.code:
// Define interfaces
INTERFACE Drawable
    FUNC draw() #void
    FUNC get_bounds() #(#float, #float, #float, #float)
end

// Base shape class
CLASS Shape IMPLEMENTS Drawable
    PROTECTED x #float
    PROTECTED y #float
    PROTECTED color #str
    
    PUBLIC CONSTRUCTOR(x #float, y #float, color #str) #void
        THIS.x := x
        THIS.y := y
        THIS.color := color
    end
    
    PUBLIC FUNC move(dx #float, dy #float) #void
        THIS.x := THIS.x + dx
        THIS.y := THIS.y + dy
    end
    
    PUBLIC FUNC draw() #void
        IO:PRINT:("Drawing shape at (" + THIS.x:TO:(#str) + ", " + THIS.y:TO:(#str) + ")")
    end
end

complete.title: Functional Programming Example
complete.code:
// Functional programming with higher-order functions
FUNC process_numbers(numbers #[#int]) #void
    IO:PRINT:("Original numbers: " + numbers:TO:(#str))
    
    // Filter even numbers
    DEF evens #[#int] = numbers 
        :FILTER:(FUNC (x #int) -> x % 2 == 0)
    IO:PRINT:("Even numbers: " + evens:TO:(#str))
    
    // Square all numbers
    DEF squares #[#int] = numbers 
        :MAP:(FUNC (x #int) -> x * x)
    IO:PRINT:("Squares: " + squares:TO:(#str))
    
    // Reduce to sum
    DEF sum #int = numbers 
        :REDUCE:(FUNC (acc #int, x #int) -> acc + x, 0)
    IO:PRINT:("Sum: " + sum:TO:(#str))
end

naming: Use descriptive variable and function names
Follow camelCase for variables and functions
Use PascalCase for classes and types
types: Use specific types over #any when possible
Prefer immutable data structures when appropriate
functions: Use function overloading for related operations
error_handling: Use specific error types for different error conditions
Always clean up resources in FINALLY blocks
concurrency: Use cancellation tokens for long-running tasks
Set appropriate timeouts for task operations
